findings.title: Plan-assigned config scope (grid resolution, layer selection) silently dropped
findings.description: The parent slice-plan entry for 304 (item 5 in `300-slices.worldserver-foundation.md`) explicitly assigns: "Server-side environment configuration (seed, **grid resolution**, layer selection) in YAML." This slice delivers only `seed` and excludes the other two: "Grid resolution configuration — no grids until layers exist," and layer selection is nowhere in scope. The doc's justification ("no grids until layers exist") is defensible for grid resolution, since 500-arch makes resolution per-layer/per-instance and routes it through the environment specification (507) — but deferring a requirement the plan entry assigns to this slice is a scope deferral that should be recorded as a decision (e.g., explicitly moving grid resolution and layer selection to 507/the layer slices, or noting the plan needs amending), not listed as a bare exclusion. As written, the slice plan and this design disagree about who delivers that configuration surface.

findings.title: Post-tick write pathway reduced to a bare `post_tick()` call
findings.description: The plan assigns this slice: "Handle post-tick environment writes (e.g., stigmergic trail deposits)." The design calls `post_tick()` with no arguments, and the Data Flow section shows no source for `trail_deposits` or `threat_mutations` at all. The 500 architecture describes the write-back as the behavior engine "returning threat zone mutations ... alongside updated agent state," but 303's `engine.tick()` has no such return contract and this slice adds none. So the slice that the plan names as responsible for the write pathway delivers only a no-arg call, without stating who computes the writes, how they reach `post_tick()`, or that this plumbing is explicitly owned by a named future slice. "Environment-aware behavioral forces — initiative 100" (Excluded) covers force construction, not the deposits/mutations plumbing. This should be addressed either by extending the design (define the handoff) or by an explicit deferral naming the slice that owns it.

findings.title: Environment context not passed to `engine.tick()`, contradicting the plan and the 500 integration surface
findings.description: Both the plan ("Pass environment context to `SimulationManager` **and `engine.tick()`**") and the 500 docs (500-arch: "The world server passes the environment (or its query method) to `engine.tick()` as the 'environmental context' parameter"; 500 slice: "The `query` method (or the `Environment` object itself) is passed to `engine.tick()` as environmental context") expect the environment to flow into `engine.tick()`. This slice instead routes the reference via force constructor injection, with `engine.tick(state, profiles, spatial, dt, forces)` unchanged and no environment parameter. That is a coherent alternative, but it changes the cross-initiative integration contract without acknowledging the conflict — the 500 initiative's stated integration surface (three methods "plus the constructor ... the complete integration surface," with context delivered to `engine.tick()`) will mislead the 501+ slices and the 100-band force work if they read the plan/500-arch. The design should state explicitly that it deliberately deviates from the "pass to `engine.tick()`" pattern and what that implies for the 500/100 contracts, or conform.

findings.title: "Layers register themselves ... plug in without server changes" conflicts with 500's composition model
findings.description: The Integration Points section claims: "Slices 501-507 add layers to the environment. The server creates the environment; layers register themselves," and the Overview claims layers "plug in without server changes." The 500 design says the opposite on both counts: layers are "composed at construction" via the `Environment(bounds, layers)` dict (the container "iterates registered layers" it was given), and 500-arch is explicit that "The environment layer does not provide a dynamic layer registry or abstract plugin interface. Layers are statically composed in the environment container." When 501 lands, `server.py` must change to construct the terrain layer and pass it into the constructor (eventually via an environment specification). The "no server changes" claim is false and risks leaving 304 with a handoff story that no 500 slice will match. The doc should describe the actual handoff: layer slices add construction code (or a spec) that the server startup wires into `Environment(bounds, layers=...)`.

findings.title: Tick-budget NFR not restated for the newly instrumented tick path
findings.description: The parent architecture states target tick rates (20–60Hz) and discusses tick-budget overrun handling; slice 301 established the tick budget and overrun metrics. This slice inserts `pre_tick()` and `post_tick()` into the per-tick path — calls that, once real layers exist, do O(active cells) work per tick (trail decay alone) plus batch-bound validation. The design adds no restatement of the tick-budget target (e.g., 50ms at 20Hz) nor any statement of how environment lifecycle work is expected to fit within it. Even with an empty environment today the cost is near-zero, but the slice's stated promise is that 501+ layers plug in without server changes, which means the budget interaction of `pre_tick`/`post_tick` should be at least acknowledged with the specific target inherited from the architecture.

findings.title: `seasonal_parameter=0.0` is mislabeled as "mid-season"
findings.description: The doc says the fixed 0.0 default produces a "mid-season" environment. Per 308/500 the seasonal parameter is a continuous 0–1 cycle value advancing per tick, so 0.0 is the *start* of the cycle, not mid-season. Harmless while layers are empty, but the label will mislead the 308 and 504 authors; correct it to "season-start (0.0)." Relatedly, the new `pre_tick`/`post_tick` call paths have no failure-mode discussion: with zero layers they cannot raise, so this is acceptable today, but one sentence on what happens if a registered layer later raises (propagate through the tick body? crash? — cf. 301's tick loop and the "no silent failures" principle) would close the gap cheaply.
